speaker: Narrator
en: Now onto the show.

speaker: Daniel Whitenack
en: Welcome to another episode of Practical AI Podcast. This is Daniel Whitenack. I am CEO at Prediction Guard, and I'm joined as always by my cohost, Benson, who is a principal AI and autonomy research engineer. How are you doing, Chris?
zh: 欢迎收听又一期的 Practical AI 播客。我是 Daniel Whitenack。我是 Prediction Guard 的 CEO，和往常一样，我的联合主持人 Benson 也在，他是一位 AI 与自主系统首席研究工程师。Chris，你今天怎么样？

speaker: Chris Benson
en: Hey. Hey. I'm doing great today, Daniel. Really excited about today's conversation.
zh: 嘿。嘿。我今天状态很好，Daniel。对今天的对话真的非常期待。

speaker: Daniel Whitenack
en: Yeah. Well, I I think in in, in the world that both of us inhabit, we are open to interesting discussions. And, I I think we'll talk about things open and things related to the world in in today's episode because we have with us MingYu Liu, who is vice president of Cosmos Lab at NVIDIA. Welcome to the show, MingYu.
zh: 是的。嗯，我……我想在我们所处的这个世界里，我们对有趣的讨论持开放态度。而且我……我想在今天的节目中我们会谈到开放相关的话题，以及与这个世界相关的事情，因为我们邀请到了 NVIDIA Cosmos 实验室副总裁 MingYu Liu。欢迎来到节目，MingYu。

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: Hello. Thanks to have me here. Great to be here. Hi, Daniel and Chris.
zh: 你好。感谢邀请我来这里。很高兴来到这里。嗨，Daniel 和 Chris。

speaker: Daniel Whitenack
en: Yeah. Yeah. Great great to have you. And one of the things I kind of alluded to is maybe something open, which I know is dear to NVIDIA's heart, which is open models. And I've seen in the news recently in what NVIDIA has posted, obviously, they are promoting open models as a key piece of what is important in the e AI ecosystem.
zh: 是的。是的。非常高兴有你来。我刚才略微提到的一件事，可能是与开放有关的东西，我知道这对 NVIDIA 来说至关重要，那就是开放模型。我最近在新闻中看到，在 NVIDIA 发布的内容中，显然，他们正在把开放模型作为 AI 生态系统中重要组成部分来推广。

speaker: Daniel Whitenack
en: I'm wondering, MingYu, if you could help us understand maybe from your perspective, from NVIDIA's perspective, why in today's, world, is open is the idea of having open models and promoting open models, why is that such a critical thing in the ecosystem?
zh: 我想知道，MingYu，你能否从你的视角、从 NVIDIA 的视角帮助我们理解，在当今的世界里，开放——也就是拥有开放模型并推广开放模型的这一理念——为什么在生态系统中如此关键？

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: Yes. Okay. So when I was a student, I learned a lot about computer vision and machine learning. At that time, there are great researchers, students, open source layer code and model. And looking at layer code and model actually help me understand the concept and help me to innovate.
zh: 好的。是这样的。当我还是学生的时候，我学了很多计算机视觉和机器学习的知识。那个时候，有很多优秀的研究者、学生，开放源代码和模型。而研究这些源代码和模型实际上帮助我理解了概念，并帮助我进行创新。

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: Right? And and this the academy always work like that and has been years, you know, even before GBT, and GBT also have open source model in the past. And that had been, you know, pushed the field forward around innovation. It's just until recently, the model is getting bigger. The amount of resources required to build a model is tremendous amount, and hence, the amount of open model reduced.
zh: 对吧？而学术界一直是这样运作的，已经很多年了，你知道，甚至在 GBT 之前，而 GBT 过去也有开源模型。这一直在推动这个领域围绕创新向前发展。只是直到最近，模型变得越来越大。构建一个模型所需的资源量是巨大的，因此，开放模型的数量减少了。

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: Right? But open model generally is there for the field, it's been very useful to push the field forward. And so, NVIDIA, won't this continue to happen? I think the world will be in a better place if we have open model to enable innovation. So people you know, API are great.
zh: 对吧？但开放模型总体上是为了这个领域而存在的，它对推动领域向前发展一直非常有用。所以，NVIDIA 希望这种情况继续下去。我认为如果我们有开放模型来促进创新，世界会变得更美好。所以人们……你知道，API 很好。

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: They solve problems, but they don't give you the insight. You know, it doesn't tell you it it doesn't allow you to tear apart and miss your idea inside. You know? And also, the the kind of thing you want to do may be suitable, you know, you want to have a local computer and you don't have the Internet connection, so API may not always be the solution. And that's why, you know, I think an open model is important to enable people.
zh: 它们能解决问题，但它们不会给你洞察。你知道，它不会告诉你，它不允许你把它拆开、把你的想法放进去。你知道？另外，你想做的事情可能适合……你知道，你可能想要本地计算，而没有互联网连接，所以 API 并不总是解决方案。这就是为什么，你知道，我认为开放模型对于赋能人们很重要。

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: And NVIDIA is a accelerator computing company. So we build this computer, great computer, GPU networking devices, and now we also build CPU, SoC. Right? We build this computer and we want to enable the whole ecosystem. Right?
zh: 而 NVIDIA 是一家加速计算公司。所以我们制造这些计算机，很棒的计算机，GPU 和网络设备，现在我们也制造 CPU、SoC。对吧？我们制造这些计算机，我们想要赋能整个生态系统。对吧？

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: And we generally believe that, you know, to better build these computers, we need to know more about the applications. Right? And in the old day, you have this computer and you have library and you have software applications, right? And in the modern world, you have computer and you have library still, but you now have models. Model is a new kind of libraries people can use and to build great amazing applications.
zh: 而我们普遍相信，你知道，为了更好地制造这些计算机，我们需要更多地了解应用。对吧？在过去，你有计算机，你有库，你有软件应用，对吧？而在现代世界，你有计算机，你仍然有库，但现在你有了模型。模型是一种新的库，人们可以使用它来构建了不起的、精彩的应用。

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: You know, maybe all kind of agents to help you buy stuff or help you do code all on top of models. And and we, like to build models, like to build open models on top of NVIDIA's computer. There are a couple of reason why we do that. First, we through building the model, we better understand what kind of computer we should build, what kind of GPU architecture we should have, so that NVIDIA can always be there to help the whole ecosystem. And second, we also want to measure people are enabled to do amazing applications, right?
zh: 你知道，也许是各种帮你买东西或帮你写代码的智能体，全都构建在模型之上。而我们，喜欢构建模型，喜欢在 NVIDIA 的计算机之上构建开放模型。我们这么做有几个原因。第一，通过构建模型，我们能更好地理解我们应该构建什么样的计算机、我们应该拥有什么样的 GPU 架构，这样 NVIDIA 才能始终在那里帮助整个生态系统。第二，我们也希望衡量人们是否被赋能去做精彩的应用，对吧？

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: So when we have open model there, and people can test this out first, and combine them to do application good for their targeted business, And again, some familiarity, and maybe later they can build their own model. So there's a lot of reason why open model is critical, both for Academy and also for the whole industry.
zh: 所以当我们有开放模型在那里，人们可以先测试它，然后把它们组合起来，做适合他们目标业务的应用。再一次，获得一些熟悉度，也许之后他们可以构建自己的模型。所以开放模型之所以关键，无论是对学术界还是对整个行业，都有很多原因。

speaker: Daniel Whitenack
en: Yeah. You were kind of getting to a follow-up that I that I wanted to have, which is it it's important to have open models to your point to promote innovation. But I'm wondering in what you're seeing at NVIDIA, is it increasingly important also on the commercial side? So, like, for NVIDIA's customers. Right?
zh: 是的。你其实已经提到了我想要追问的一个问题，那就是，正如你所说，拥有开放模型对促进创新很重要。但我想知道，从你在 NVIDIA 所看到的情况来看，在商业方面，这是否也变得越来越重要？比如说，对 NVIDIA 的客户而言。对吧？

speaker: Daniel Whitenack
en: What is the implication of having access to open models maybe on the on the commercial side? Do you have an do you have any thoughts on that? So it's great if, like, I'm in a lab and, you know, I have, you know, five years to to work towards, you know, the next innovation, the next types of models. But if I'm in a commercial company, maybe I'm a customer of NVIDIA, I run NVIDIA hardware, how does the existence of open models help me as, you know, in the commercial world maybe?
zh: 拥有开放模型的访问权在商业方面可能意味着什么？你对此有什么想法吗？因为，如果我在一个实验室里，你知道，我有五年时间去研究下一个创新、下一代模型，那当然很好。但如果我在一家商业公司，也许是 NVIDIA 的客户，我运行 NVIDIA 的硬件，那么开放模型的存在在商业世界里对我有什么帮助？

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: Innovation, freedom. Innovation, freedom. I think that is maybe the two words to to to summarize. Right? So, you know, you can leverage API to solve the problem.
zh: 创新，自由。创新，自由。我想这也许是可以用来总结的两个词。对吧？所以，你知道，你可以利用 API 来解决问题。

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: And but with the open model, you can do more than what's available in in API. Yeah. So and see, the the field is finding more and more important application of AI. Right? You know, from earlier day of chatbot and now the the coding agent, and we we also see more and more agent that can do things that we didn't think it's possible.
zh: 但有了开放模型，你可以做比 API 里现成的更多的事情。是的。而且你看，这个领域正在发现越来越多 AI 的重要应用。对吧？你知道，从早期的聊天机器人到现在的编码智能体，我们也看到越来越多的智能体能做到我们以前认为不可能的事情。

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: People are working very hard to try to figure out how AI can make our life collectively better. Right? And there there will be application that was not foreseen by the foundation model of the frontier companies who are building AI. Right? And they require some customization.
zh: 人们正在非常努力地尝试弄清楚 AI 如何能共同让我们的生活变得更好。对吧？而且会有一些应用，是那些构建 AI 的前沿公司的基座模型所没有预见到的。对吧？而这些应用需要一些定制化。

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: Open model allow them give them options, give them choice to do the innovation they need for their target business. And and this way, I I think it's good, for the whole society.
zh: 开放模型给了他们选择，让他们能够为自己的目标业务做所需的创新。这样一来，我认为这对整个社会都有好处。

speaker: Chris Benson
en: I think, I know I was kind of following up on your point there, I was very happy recently to see NVIDIA kind of there was a moment some months back where open models in the West were starting to struggle a bit, and certain unnamed organizations were closing that had been leading the way, and so it was a delight to see NVIDIA step in and take the leadership there and follow through with some other things, the Hugging Face acquisition that's coming in, the work that you're doing. We're kind of going through this turning point toward the next generation of open models and what that looks like, especially with regard to the landscape of physical AI out there, which is my personal passion, as most of our viewers know. So would love if you could kind of, as we are pivoting into this new generation of open models in physical AI context, where it's not all API based, it's not all frontier models at big services and stuff like that, and we're all getting excited about drones in everyday life, robots in everyday life, all the different capacities that that can bring benefits. Could you kind of lay landscape?
zh: 我想，我知道我在接着你的观点往下说，我最近非常高兴地看到 NVIDIA——几个月前有过一个时刻，西方的开放模型开始有点陷入困境，某些不便点名名称的曾经领先的组织正在走向封闭，所以看到 NVIDIA 挺身而出、在那里承担领导地位并践行承诺，比如即将到来的对 Hugging Face 的收购、你们正在做的工作，真是令人欣喜。我们正在经历这个转折点，走向下一代开放模型以及它将呈现的样子，尤其是关于物理 AI 的格局，这是我的个人热情所在，正如我们大多数观众所知道的。所以我很希望，当我们转向物理 AI 语境下的这一代新开放模型时——它不全是基于 API 的，不全是大型服务的前沿模型之类的，而我们都在为日常生活中的无人机、日常生活中的机器人以及它们能带来益处的各种能力而兴奋——你能否描述一下这个格局？

speaker: Chris Benson
en: As you mesh these things together, what does that look like to you now? What are you seeing as the opportunities in the near term, and kind of how are organizations that work with NVIDIA starting to position to take on this next generation of physical AI that's upon us?
zh: 当你把这些东西融合在一起时，在你看来那会是什么样子？你在近期看到了哪些机会，那些与 NVIDIA 合作的组织正在如何定位，以迎接已经到来的这一代物理 AI？

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: Yeah, thanks for the great question. So I think physical AI is a term covers several important verticals. Automotive is one, factory automation is another, and robotics is sub pillar. There could be more, agriculture, construction, many of them. And physical AI are AI deployed in physical device.
zh: 是的，谢谢这个很好的问题。我认为物理 AI 是一个涵盖几个重要垂直领域的术语。汽车是一个，工厂自动化是另一个，机器人是其中一个子领域。可能还有更多，农业、建筑等等。而物理 AI 是部署在物理设备中的 AI。

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: And physical device perturb the state of the world and complete certain tasks. And the result is shown as material, as the final something you can touch, right? That is how I would like to define physical AI. So, nowadays, we have some AI in physical device, right? But they are preliminary, right?
zh: 物理设备扰动世界的状态，完成特定的任务。其结果以物质的形式呈现，作为最终你可以触摸到的东西，对吧？这就是我想要定义物理 AI 的方式。那么，如今，我们在物理设备中已经有了一些 AI，对吧？但它们还很初级，对吧？

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: And I think the most exciting form of physical AI, one of the most exciting forms of physical AI is a humanoid robot. And we envision that humanoid robot will be able to help people accomplish our task. And now we don't have humanoid robots surrounding us, but one day we have humanoid robots surrounding us, they will require a computer. They will require a powerful computer to help us process visual input, understand people's instruction, and then self correction in completed tasks. And these are great business opportunity for NVIDIA.
zh: 而我认为物理 AI 最令人兴奋的形式之一，就是人形机器人。我们设想人形机器人将能够帮助人们完成任务。现在我们周围还没有人形机器人，但有一天当我们周围有人形机器人时，它们将需要一台计算机。它们将需要一台强大的计算机来帮助我们处理视觉输入、理解人的指令，然后对未完成的任务进行自我纠正。而这些是 NVIDIA 了不起的商业机会。

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: Right? So that's why NVIDIA care about Physical AI. If we can make Physical AI come, you know, the the dream of Physical AI come true, there will be allow opportunity for media. So we are very aligned. And so we want to help the field moving forward.
zh: 对吧？所以这就是 NVIDIA 关心物理 AI 的原因。如果我们能让物理 AI、物理 AI 的梦想成真，将会给 NVIDIA 带来大量机会。所以我们是非常一致的。因此我们想要帮助这个领域向前发展。

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: Yeah. Yeah. Go ahead.
zh: 是的。是的。你请说。

speaker: Daniel Whitenack
en: Yeah. And I was wondering, just tying that back to where we started the conversation with open models, do open models have certain implications specifically in the physical AI world because of the constraints or requirements of the physical AI world?
zh: 是的。我想知道，把这和我们对话开始时谈到的开放模型联系起来，开放模型是否因为物理 AI 世界的约束或需求，而在物理 AI 世界中有某些特定的影响？

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: Yes. That's a good question. So I think, for example, one thing you a Physical AI model, you know, one popular Physical AI model is a policy model. A policy model is a model based on the visual observation and the interaction given by the user or some machine. And, you know, that it generates an action to complete the task.
zh: 是的。这是个好问题。我认为，举例来说，有一件事……一种物理 AI 模型，你知道，一种流行的物理 AI 模型是策略模型。策略模型是一种基于视觉观测以及用户或某台机器给出的交互的模型。你知道，它会生成一个动作来完成任务。

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: Right? So observation, instruction in and action out. And every robot have a different kind of sensor setup. Right? Some robot have two eyes.
zh: 对吧？所以观测和指令输入，动作输出。而每个机器人都有一套不同的传感器配置。对吧？有些机器人有两只眼睛。

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: Some robot have cameras mounted on the gripper. And self driving car, some car has 11 cameras. Some have seven. You know? Some have LiDAR sensor.
zh: 有些机器人在夹爪上安装了摄像头。而自动驾驶汽车，有些车有 11 个摄像头，有些有 7 个。你知道？有些有 LiDAR 传感器。

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: So every physical device, every physical every robot see the world differently. Right? And and some of them are unique. Right? And so it's difficult to have one AI model that can cover all of these.
zh: 所以每个物理设备、每个机器人看世界的方式都不同。对吧？而且其中一些是独特的。对吧？所以很难有一个 AI 模型能覆盖所有这些情况。

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: Right? And when you have open model, the model come with viewing capability, like a word understanding or simulation. And from that prior, people can leverage the data they collected from their device and fine tune. You know, maybe this in the initial model only handle one camera. Now you have multi view, you know, enabled through post training and open model.
zh: 对吧？而当你有开放模型时，这个模型自带一定的能力，比如语言理解或仿真。从这个先验出发，人们可以利用他们从自己设备上收集的数据进行微调。你知道，也许这个初始模型只处理一个摄像头，现在你通过后训练和开放模型实现了多视角。

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: And it's easier it's more achievable with open model. Right? So I think open model give you the the innovation power. So you can customize open model to better tailor for your physical use case. This is important.
zh: 而有了开放模型，这更容易实现、更可达成。对吧？所以我认为开放模型给你创新的力量。这样你就可以定制开放模型，让它更好地适配你的物理用例。这很重要。

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: Right? It means better leverage the observation. Right? And it also give you opportunity to make it more efficient. Yeah.
zh: 对吧？这意味着更好地利用观测。对吧？而且它也给你机会让它变得更高效。是的。

speaker: Ming-Yu Liu
en: So in the end, the primary evolution will be intelligence per per watt. Right? And and so with this open architecture, you will be able to do more.
zh: 所以归根结底，主要的进化方向将是每瓦特智能。对吧？而有了这种开放架构，你将能够做得更多。
